Claim: The Trump administration declared that erecting a White House ballroom is the president's main priority (over cost of living, health care, or reopening government).
Ended: Oct 24, 2025 (PolitiFact False: Leavitt answered about renovation priorities only)
Who_Pushed_It: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries; House Democratic Caucus; Democratic National Committee; Sen. Chuck Schumer (amplifying clipped clip)
Notes: Leavitt's 'main priority' answer was about White House construction projects, not all presidential priorities.

Claim: Republicans have 'effectively ended medical research in the United States of America' via Trump's second-term NIH and research cuts.
Ended: Sep 29, 2025 (PolitiFact Mostly False: proposed NIH budget would still be ~$27B; appropriations panels rejected steep cuts)
Who_Pushed_It: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries
Approximate_Duration: about 5 days until Mostly False rating
Notes: Real steep proposed cuts and grant terminations existed; 'effectively ended' overstated remaining funding and congressional pushback.

Claim: When Biden took office, the Trump administration had contracted for 'not nearly enough' COVID vaccine to cover U.S. adults.
Ended: Mar 5, 2021 (PolitiFact Mostly False: Warp Speed portfolio contracts covered far more than the adult population if cleared)
Who_Pushed_It: President Joe Biden
Notes: Authorized Pfizer/Moderna doses alone were short of all adults; total Warp Speed contracts were much larger.

Claim: The process to distribute COVID vaccine to the broader community 'did not really exist' when the Biden team entered the White House.
Ended: Jan 27, 2021 (PolitiFact Mostly False: a state-led federal distribution plan existed despite flaws)
Who_Pushed_It: White House Chief of Staff Ron Klain (Meet the Press)
Notes: Experts criticized communication and funding gaps; 'did not really exist' overstated a real state-centric plan.

Claim: When President Biden took office there was 'no vaccine available' for COVID-19 (implying Trump left Americans with none).
Ended: May 13, 2022 (White House corrected tweet); May 16, 2022 (PolitiFact False)
Who_Pushed_It: The White House (@WhiteHouse under Biden)
Notes: 20M+ doses administered under Trump; Biden himself vaccinated Dec 2020. Correction: 'not widely available.'

Claim: In Trump's first year back he created only about 185,000 jobs total (versus 2.2 million in Biden's last year).
Ended: Mar 5, 2026 (FactCheck.org: Biden inflated his figure and undersold Trump; ~359,000 Jan 2025–Jan 2026)
Who_Pushed_It: Former President Joe Biden (South Carolina Democratic Party event)
Notes: Relied on outdated/revision-sensitive BLS figures after annual revisions lowered Biden-era estimates.

Claim: The U.S. economy experienced 'record growth' during the Biden administration (used as a contrast with Trump).
Ended: Mar 5, 2026 (FactCheck.org: no basis; higher growth under other presidents/eras)
Who_Pushed_It: Former President Joe Biden
Approximate_Duration: same speech cycle as jobs claim
Notes: Highest Biden quarterly ~7% in 2021 rebound; WWII and other eras higher.

Claim: Melania Trump was 'very involved' in Trump's Epstein relationship / was introduced to Trump via a modeling agent connected to Jeffrey Epstein.
Ended: Jul 2025 (article removed); Sep 10–15, 2025 (updated Daily Beast apology to Melania)
Who_Pushed_It: The Daily Beast (based on Michael Wolff interview/podcast)
Approximate_Duration: weeks from publication to apology update
Notes: Outlet said article did not meet standards; Melania memoir describes Kit Kat Klub meeting.

Claim: There was an 'Epstein connection' involving Melania Trump and Donald Trump (as framed in Carville's YouTube title and comments).
Ended: Aug 8, 2025 (Carville apology; video removed; comments edited out)
Who_Pushed_It: James Carville (Democratic strategist; Politics War Room)
Approximate_Duration: about 1 week until apology after Melania's lawyer letter
Notes: Carville: 'I also take back these statements and apologize.' Distinct from Daily Beast article.

Claim: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer was notified of Trump's Iran nuclear-site strikes only after the attack (Democrats not informed in advance).
Ended: Jun 22–23, 2025 (CNN correction: Schumer was called before the strike)
Who_Pushed_It: CNN (initial report); similar framing amplified elsewhere including MSNBC critiques of notification
Notes: CNN updated that Schumer was called ~1 hour before strikes; Jeffries reached later.

Claim: Donald Trump was on the phone urging Israeli PM Netanyahu not to agree to a Gaza ceasefire because a deal would help Kamala Harris's campaign.
Ended: Aug 21, 2024 (Judy Woodruff apology; Trump and Netanyahu offices denied)
Who_Pushed_It: Judy Woodruff (PBS News); American Muckrakers PAC complaint citing her remarks
Notes: Snopes rated underlying call content Unproven; Woodruff apologized for repeating a denied characterization. Axios added Netanyahu denial note.

Claim: Penn Wharton / 'Wharton School' determined Harris's plan would strengthen the economy and Trump's would weaken it.
Ended: Sep 27, 2024 (FactCheck.org: PWBM found Harris plan reduces GDP more than Trump's)
Who_Pushed_It: Vice President Kamala Harris
Notes: PWBM: both plans raise deficits; Harris GDP hit larger. Distinct from tariff $4,000 Half True ratings.

Claim: Goldman Sachs said Harris's plan would grow the economy and Trump's would shrink it.
Ended: Sep 27, 2024 (FactCheck.org: Goldman modeled continued growth under both; Trump scenario slower growth, not shrinkage)
Who_Pushed_It: Vice President Kamala Harris
Notes: Goldman CEO said difference was about two-tenths of a percent.

Claim: Trump will give billionaires 'another round of tax breaks that will add up to $5 trillion to the national debt' (framed as a billionaire-only giveaway).
Ended: Aug 23, 2024 (FactCheck.org: figure is cost of extending TCJA cuts that benefited all income groups)
Who_Pushed_It: Vice President Kamala Harris; Democratic National Convention messaging
Approximate_Duration: DNC week and subsequent campaign use
Notes: Extending TCJA is costly; 'billionaires' framing omits broad individual-rate benefits.

Claim: Trump announced a budget to cut Social Security and Medicare every single year he was in office (as benefit cuts for seniors).
Ended: Aug 19, 2024 (Washington Post Fact Checker: budgets did not seek cuts to SS retirement benefits; Medicare items largely provider-payment reforms)
Who_Pushed_It: Harris-Walz campaign (tweet labeled 'Fact')
Notes: Distinct from 2024 'intends to cut' items 44–46; this is about every past Trump budget as benefit cuts.

Claim: Harris said Trump 'tried to cut Social Security and Medicare' in his presidential budgets (as cuts to seniors' retirement/Medicare benefits).
Ended: Aug 23, 2024 (FactCheck.org: budgets did not propose cutting SS retirement benefits; Medicare proposals largely provider-payment reforms)
Who_Pushed_It: Vice President Kamala Harris; Sen. Tammy Baldwin (related CNBC 'cutting' quote framing)
Approximate_Duration: DNC week with long prior Mediscare variants
Notes: About first-term budgets but pushed in 2024. Distinct from 'intends to cut' items 44–46 and every-year budget tweet.

Claim: The Supreme Court ruled that Trump 'would be immune from criminal prosecution' (absolute-immunity framing).
Ended: Aug 23, 2024 (FactCheck.org: Court held a presumption of immunity for official acts, not immunity for unofficial acts)
Who_Pushed_It: Vice President Kamala Harris (DNC acceptance speech)
Notes: Roberts: president has no immunity for unofficial acts; not everything is official.

Claim: Trump 'encouraged Putin to invade' a NATO ally / invited Russia to 'do whatever the hell they want' (omitting the NATO dues-delinquency condition).
Ended: Aug 23, 2024 (FactCheck.org: Trump said he told a delinquent NATO member he would not protect it unless bills were paid)
Who_Pushed_It: Kamala Harris; Sen. Mark Kelly; former Defense Secretary Leon Panetta (DNC speakers)
Approximate_Duration: months of truncated clip use; DNC spike Aug 2024
Notes: Still aggressive rhetoric; Democrats omitted the stated condition about delinquent NATO spending.

Claim: The Philadelphia Eagles declined / gave a 'massive no' to a White House invitation to celebrate their Super Bowl win with Trump.
Ended: Feb 24, 2025 (PolitiFact False: White House said no invitation had yet been extended)
Who_Pushed_It: The U.S. Sun; Newsweek (amplifying reported snub); viral social posts
Approximate_Duration: about 2 weeks of premature snub narrative
Notes: Unfavorable 'snubbed Trump' framing before any invite existed.

Claim: Trump reversed all Biden-negotiated Medicare/Medicaid drug price caps, raising prescription costs by as much as 4,200%.
Ended: Feb 28, 2025 (USA TODAY False: IRA caps are statute; executive order did not remove them)
Who_Pushed_It: Tristan Snell (political commentator/attorney on X); Facebook recirculation
Approximate_Duration: about 5–6 weeks until USA TODAY False
Notes: Trump rescinded a Biden EO directing CMS Innovation Center consideration; insulin/vaccine caps are in the Inflation Reduction Act.

Claim: President Trump said Israel's assassination campaign of Iranian leaders was complicating U.S. negotiations with Iran (paraphrase/truncation).
Ended: Jul 13, 2026 (Washington Post correction: Trump did not directly mention Israel; quote improperly truncated)
Who_Pushed_It: The Washington Post
Notes: CAMERA documented WaPo correction restoring fuller quote without Israel attribution.

Claim: The Trump administration was 'raiding money' from military service members' pensions to fund the border wall.
Ended: Mar 28, 2019 (PolitiFact False: leftover personnel funds; no pension cuts)
Who_Pushed_It: Sen. Kamala Harris
Notes: Harris linked an AP headline; defense-budget experts said no service member would lose pension payments.

Claim: Ohio, Michigan, and Pennsylvania 'in the latest jobs data have lost jobs, not gained them' under Trump.
Ended: Oct 16, 2019 (PolitiFact False: latest month-to-month BLS showed gains; Castro cherry-picked March–July)
Who_Pushed_It: Julián Castro (Democratic debate)
Notes: Year-over-year and since-inauguration employment rose in all three states.

Claim: The U.S. under Trump currently had more than 100,000 children in migration-related detention (world's highest rate).
Ended: Nov 19–20, 2019 (AFP/Reuters withdrew; UN expert clarified figure was cumulative 2015/Obama-era, not current)
Who_Pushed_It: AFP; Reuters; NPR pickup; House Homeland Security Committee Democrats; Sen. Bernie Sanders (tweet later deleted)
Notes: Contemporaneous ORR/family detention numbers were far lower (~thousands).

Claim: President Trump spent Thanksgiving 2019 tweeting and golfing at Mar-a-Lago rather than visiting U.S. troops.
Ended: Nov 28, 2019 evening (Newsweek substantially updated); reporter later fired / editor demoted
Who_Pushed_It: Newsweek (Jessica Kwong)
Approximate_Duration: hours until update after Afghanistan trip became public
Notes: Trip was secret until return; Kwong called pre-announcement reporting an 'honest mistake.'

Claim: Trump chose not to listen to the translation of the Italian prime minister's speech at the G7 (shown without large headphones).
Ended: May 27, 2017 (BBC correspondent James Landale corrected within ~30 minutes; White House: single in-ear piece)
Who_Pushed_It: BBC Diplomatic Correspondent James Landale; amplified by other journalists' retweets
Approximate_Duration: under an hour until correction; original tweet far more viral
Notes: Spicer later cited the viral false framing; Landale acknowledged the earpiece explanation.

Claim: Children of U.S. troops born overseas would no longer automatically get U.S. citizenship under a Trump/USCIS policy change (as broadly framed).
Ended: Aug 28–29, 2019 (NBC correction; USCIS/Military Times clarified narrow adoption/noncitizen-parent cases)
Who_Pushed_It: Tal Kopan (San Francisco Chronicle); Task & Purpose; NBC News (Ken Dilanian initial tweets before correction)
Approximate_Duration: hours of viral panic until corrections
Notes: Did not end birthright citizenship for children of U.S. citizen service members; AP said ~20–25 cases/year affected.

Claim: Arizona Republic used 2014 photos of migrant children in holding facilities as if depicting then-current Trump-era detention conditions.
Ended: May 27–28, 2018 (azcentral clarification that photos were from 2014)
Who_Pushed_It: The Arizona Republic / azcentral
Notes: Related theme to NYT Magazine cage RT (v2) but distinct outlet correction listed by Poynter.

Claim: Trump's tax cut was 'a middle-class tax hike' evidenced by average tax refunds being down about $170.
Ended: Feb 13, 2019 (PolitiFact Mostly False: early refund drop ≠ higher tax burden; most middle-class households projected tax cuts)
Who_Pushed_It: Sen. Kamala Harris
Notes: Refund size depends on withholding; WaPo Fact Checker also criticized the leap.

Claim: Donald Trump 'just promised that if he wins reelection, he'll gut Social Security and Medicare.'
Ended: Aug 13, 2020 (PolitiFact Mostly False: no such promise; payroll-tax deferral did not affect Medicare funding)
Who_Pushed_It: Sen. Kamala Harris (Instagram)
Approximate_Duration: days around Aug 2020 payroll-tax EO debate
Notes: Distinct from excluded staging FT-9 (Social Security Works 'terminate') and from 2024 'intends to cut' items 44–46. Trump discussed payroll-tax permanence, not gutting benefits.

Claim: Trump 'signed an executive action directing funding cuts for Social Security' and 'proposed slashing hundreds of billions of dollars from the Social Security Trust Fund every year' / 'promised to defund Social Security.'
Ended: Aug 14, 2020 (PolitiFact Ad Watch: Biden exaggerates; deferral ≠ benefit cut; White House disputed 'terminate tax' meaning)
Who_Pushed_It: Joe Biden campaign (Florida TV ad; Tampa Bay Times op-ed)
Approximate_Duration: days of Florida ad buy around Aug 2020
Notes: Distinct from excluded FT-9 terminate meme and from 2024 intends-to-cut items. Legitimate solvency questions about payroll-tax talk; ad overstated 'directing funding cuts' / 'defund.'
